candidateAnswers.argumentAgainst: A hamlet of 300 people and a city of 90,000 draw from the same band, so small towns get councils as large as mid-sized cities.
candidateAnswers.argumentFor: Already built, stable per town, drawn only from councils the game has actually read.
candidateAnswers.label: Keep the read councils' middle band
candidateAnswers.position: An unread town's seat count is drawn from the middle half of the read councils' sizes (7 to 12 today) and its term from every read term.

candidateAnswers.argumentAgainst: Needs a national distribution by population band that the game does not have.
candidateAnswers.argumentFor: A village gets a village board and a city a city council, as in the real country.
candidateAnswers.label: Draw by population band
candidateAnswers.position: An unread town's seat count and term are drawn from a national distribution for towns of its population band, with any state that fixes them by general law overriding the draw.

notes: Measured on branch claude/project-thread-l04zry: 19,462 towns are offered a governing body; 60 have a compiled government and 39 of those state a seat count or term. Every other town is given a PLACEHOLDER: seats drawn from the middle half of the read sizes (7 to 12) and a term from every read term (mostly 2 years, some 3 and 4). The placeholder is marked in code (src/simulation/nationwide-world/local-governing-body-rules.ts) and labelled as typical on the office screen.

The read councils are mostly cities, so the placeholder is biased toward city-sized bodies. Presque Isle ME (pop. about 9,000) draws 7 seats and 4-year terms; a village of a few hundred would draw the same range.
question: When the game has not read a town's charter, how many seats should its governing body have and how long should the terms run, given the town's population? Is there a national distribution of council or board size and term length by population band, and which states fix either by general municipal law for all their municipalities?

sourcesChecked.source: The 39 compiled municipal governments whose readings state a body size or term
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Nearly all are cities; they say nothing about villages and small towns.

title: How big a town's council is, by town size
usableAnswer: For each population band (for example under 1,000; 1,000 to 10,000; 10,000 to 50,000; over 50,000), a range or shares of governing-body size and of term length, plus the states whose general law fixes size or term for every municipality, with the instrument named. Unknown stays marked unknown.
whyItMatters: Every unread town, which is nearly all of them, shows a council size and term on the office screen, and a council's size decides how many colleagues vote with or against a member.
